name: Pakistan

findings.controller: Huawei Marine Networks (lead contractor); PEACE Cable International Network Co. (Hengtong Group subsidiary)
findings.summary: The PEACE submarine cable's Karachi-to-Marseille route became ready for service in August 2022 after the Pakistan-Egypt segment's final splice; Cybernet is the Pakistan landing partner and built the Karachi landing station, landed in March 2021.
findings.analyst_inference: Cable owner is a Hong Kong-registered Hengtong subsidiary and the lead contractor was Huawei Marine (now HMN Tech) per Converge Digest's 2018 item; the vendor attribution rests on that one source, while RFS status is corroborated by two hosts. Pole prc because both supplier and owner-operator are PRC firms.

findings.summary: Ericsson and Jazz signed a five-year microwave frame contract for MINI-LINK backhaul equipment and services, aimed at adding capacity, extending rural coverage and preparing the backbone for 4G expansion and 5G.
findings.analyst_inference: Microwave transport only; Jazz's RAN and core vendors are not named. TelecomTV is a verbatim republication of the Ericsson release and APP is the state news agency (S4), so it is not counted as corroborated; medium rests on the opened Ericsson S1 release. Ericsson is Swedish, so the pole is third. Value undisclosed.

findings.controller: Quantum Global Data Center (QGDC, Gul Ahmed Energy Group venture)
findings.local_actor: Gul Ahmed Energy Group; Karachi Technopolis
findings.builder: Huawei Technologies Pakistan (design and technical planning partner)
findings.summary: QGDC announced a US$230m initial investment, potentially rising to US$600m, in what it calls Pakistan's largest Tier III data centre in Karachi Technopolis, with 136MW captive power; ground was broken in early June 2026, operations targeted 2027.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei Pakistan signed an MoU and design agreement (May 2026) and a strategic partnership (June 2026) to provide design, technical planning and solutions; it is recorded as builder/designer and does not set the pole for a building. If Huawei turns out to supply the IT/network equipment, a separate prc equipment finding would be warranted. Capacity is reported as 80MW (IASP) or 100MW (QGDC site per DCD). Tier 4 rests on DCD's groundbreaking report.

findings.summary: Data Vault Pakistan and Telenor Pakistan launched a locally hosted sovereign AI cloud offering GPU-as-a-service; Data Vault's CEO says it has secured over 3,000 Nvidia GPUs with Nvidia approval, bought via Nvidia partners.
findings.analyst_inference: The 3,000+ GPU count and the 'approval' are the company's own claims; GPU model and any BIS licence are not documented. Tier 5 because the service is reported as launched and operating. The facility operator (Data Vault, apparently Pakistani) would be domestic; ownership is not stated in any source.

findings.summary: A Supermicro team visited Data Vault Pakistan's Karachi facility to study deploying Nvidia Blackwell-class B200/B300 GPUs and GB300 NVL72 racks; shipment would depend on US export authorisations separate from Data Vault's existing GPU approvals.
findings.analyst_inference: Feasibility study only (tier 2). Single source. Pakistan is D:4 (licence required, presumption of approval per the global layer), so this is a licensing question rather than a ban.

findings.local_actor: Government of Pakistan (inaugurated by the Prime Minister)
findings.summary: Sky47's 8.5MW 'Karakoram One' data centre and AI cloud in Islamabad, billed as Pakistan's largest, was inaugurated by the Prime Minister and army chief; Sky47 says it has deployed many GPUs and is building a 5MW Karachi site.
findings.analyst_inference: Single source from an NGO-run outlet, treated as S4. GPU vendor not named. Sky47 appears to be a Pakistani company, hence domestic; ownership not confirmed.

findings.summary: Pakistan and Google signed an MoU at a reception hosted by the Prime Minister covering free Gemini/Google AI Plus access for students, an AI Centre of Excellence in Islamabad, and exploring AI for government services including FBR digitisation and agriculture.
findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding MoU (tier 1), decays. Signing ministry and exact date not stated. Coded as models because Gemini access is the concrete AI element; no cloud hosting mentioned.

findings.summary: Huawei won Lahore's safe-city surveillance project in 2016 with a reported US$150m bid; about 8,000 cameras were installed that year. In 2021 the Punjab Safe Cities Authority examined a contractor's claims of a data-access duplicate system in China.
findings.analyst_inference: The US$150m is from a contractor's lawsuit, so not entered as a value. The 2021 data-security check was a review, not a reversal; its outcome was not found. Pre-2020: still_current not confirmed. Bloomberg also reports a ~US$100m Islamabad command centre (2016, ~1,950 cameras, about half out of order) but the vendor attribution for Islamabad was not verified in this pass, so it is not coded.

power.null_reason: only AI-adjacent power found is QGDC's 136MW captive Gul Ahmed plant, which predates the DC and is noted in PAK-003 rather than coded separately

research_gaps: Which vendors supply RAN and core for Jazz, Zong (China Mobile), Ufone/PTCL and Telenor Pakistan, especially for the 2026 5G launches after the spectrum auction? Search returned no vendor awards.
Does Huawei supply IT or network equipment (not just design) for the QGDC Karachi data centre?

Is the 2016 Huawei Lahore safe-city system still in service, and what was the outcome of the 2021 Punjab Safe Cities Authority data-security review? Confirm the vendor of the Islamabad Safe City command centre (~US$100m, 2016) and newer Punjab/Sindh safe-city expansions.
PTA suspended Huawei's unused 2017 vehicle-tracking CVAS licence (date not found); PTA said other Huawei operations continue. Not coded as a reversal; a reviewer may wish to confirm.
Has any BIS licence been granted for Nvidia GPUs to Data Vault Pakistan or Sky47, and which GPU models? GPU vendor for Sky47 is unnamed.
ZTE's reported exit from serving Pakistani operators after the 2018 US ban (TechJuice lead, not opened) and ZTE's role in the national web-monitoring firewall: verify and date.
Any sovereign Pakistani LLM or government adoption of PRC models (DeepSeek, Qwen) following WAICO founding membership.
